paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's promise doesn't need your plan to go smoothly. The night before this plot, the Lord stood near Paul and told him to "Take courage!" and that he must testify in Rome too (Acts 23:11). Then more than forty men swore an oath to kill him (Acts 23:12-13). Those two things sit side by side, and the promise is the one still standing at the end.

Now look at HOW it got done. A young man heard something, told the right person, and a commander listened (Acts 23:16-22). Nobody in this passage gets a voice from heaven or a burst of light. It's a nephew, a centurion and a letter. I spent years in a junk drawer thinking nothing was happening, and meanwhile God was already working on the next thing. So when your own days look ordinary, don't count them out.

And notice Paul. He doesn't sit on the news or wait for a miracle to land in his lap. He passes it along at once (Acts 23:17). God's plan was safe, and Paul still did the next small thing in front of him. That's a good way to bake, friend: trust Him with the big picture, then do your part with both hands, or one mustache.
